clue.text: Coordinated shots explosively end a life

indicators.note: something blown apart explosively ends up scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A burst of gunfire violently ends someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosively' shuffles END A LIFE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfilade is a volley of gunfire raking along a line of troops from end to end.

clue.text: Covered in mud, river is ruined

indicators.note: the river is covered by the mud, so it sits inside the word for mud

parts.note: silt is fine mud deposited by water
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A river choked with mud has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Covered in mud' as describing the river; really the river goes inside the mud, and 'is' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilt is a past participle meaning damaged or ruined, so 'is ruined' equals 'is spoilt'.

clue.text: Toured frozen zone, not finding river — that's instructive

parts.note: to have 'done' a country is to have toured it, so toured gives did

indicators.note: the river cannot be found in the frozen zone's word, so its letter is removed

parts.note: the Arctic is the frozen polar region in the far north

explanation.surface: An explorer crossed the polar ice but never found a river, which was a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finding' takes R out of ARCTIC, leaving ACTIC; 'that's' is part of the definition, standing for 'which is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to teach, the same as instructive.

clue.text: Rejected juice — time to take one's aperitif

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the word for juice is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant
one is I, and one's is short for one is, giving I plus IS

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a fruit juice: time for a proper pre-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' is the reversal signal; 'to take' are just joining words, and 'one's' is read as 'one is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed spirit from France, drunk diluted as a pre-dinner drink.

clue.text: Gypsy might be one putting lots of money before cashier

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
a bank teller is a cashier

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a great deal of cash at a bank counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the money ahead of the cashier.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany gypsies are traditionally pictured reading palms and predicting futures for customers.

clue.text: Stunner, given difficult question, missing the first point

indicators.note: the point is missing from the word for a hard question, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a teaser is a tricky puzzle or question
E (east) comes first among the compass points in many listings of crossword point letters

explanation.surface: Someone gorgeous is asked a tough question and misses the opening point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes an E (a compass point) from TEASER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun, so literally a device that stuns.

clue.text: Try facial hair? It's a pain

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
tache is informal for moustache

explanation.surface: Should I grow a moustache? Too much bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional pain or sorrow.

clue.text: To manipulate digger across a road at first a complicated procedure

parts.note: to rig a result is to manipulate it

indicators.note: the digger stretches across the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: a mole is an animal that digs tunnels

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word road is used

explanation.surface: Someone tries to steer a mechanical digger over a road, which is a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts A and R (the first letter of 'road', from 'at first') inside MOLE, giving MOARLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, fussy, complicated process.

clue.text: Smart chap Geneva's got drunk?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs, so the final hiss of the word comes out as a sh sound

parts.note: a man from Geneva is Swiss

explanation.surface: A dapper man from Geneva has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got drunk' slurs the last S of SWISS into an H.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable or stylish, like smart.

clue.text: Fruit: gorilla ate part, mostly messily

indicators.note: a messy eater scatters things, so these letters are jumbled
most of the word part is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A gorilla ate some of the fruit, sloppily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PART to PAR; 'messily' shuffles GORILLAATE plus PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Alligator pear is an old name for the avocado, a fruit.

clue.text: For writer, a sort of card half-completed

parts.note: a SIM card is the chip card in a mobile phone

indicators.note: only half of the word for completed is kept, losing its back two letters

parts.note: over means finished or completed

explanation.surface: A writer has a card only half filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts OVER to OV.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific American science-fiction writer.

clue.text: Cutback has appeal with one business minister perhaps

parts.note: the word splits into a verb meaning lop followed by back, which turns that verb round
it is old slang for sex appeal
I is the Roman numeral for one
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A spending cut is popular with a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Cutback' must be split: 'Cut' (LOP) plus 'back', the reversal signal turning it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician, and a government minister is one example.

clue.text: Strip turning greying-brown in river

indicators.note: the turned colour goes inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: turning makes the colour word read backwards

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A strip of land turns a dull brown in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales and England; 'Strip' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip something bare.

clue.text: Corresponding, so we hear, since child needs a good book?

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
a son is a child
NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book, the Bible

explanation.surface: Since a child needs a good book to read?
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonant describes words whose vowel sounds match, so they correspond to the ear.

clue.text: Discussion finished, time for little one to sleep?

definitions.meaning: the phrase says there is nothing more to discuss

definitions.text: time for little one to sleep?
definitions.meaning: a bedtime tale ends and the child goes to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase closes an argument, and literally the last words of a bedtime tale.

clue.text: One likely to lose intensity shortly?

definitions.text: One likely to lose intensity shortly?

indicators.note: shortly cuts off the last letter of the word for losing intensity

parts.note: to fade is to grow dim or weaker

explanation.surface: Something soon set to weaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts FADE to FAD, and the whole clue also describes a craze, which soon fades.
explanation.definitionFit: A fad is a short-lived craze whose popularity soon dwindles.

clue.text: In speaking, one without polish

indicators.note: in speech the words sound like another word

parts.note: someone who lacks something is a lacker

explanation.surface: Talking, someone lacks refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: LACKER and LACQUER sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hard glossy varnish, a polish for wood.

clue.text: Crush opposition to proposal for type of restaurant

definitions.meaning: to push a plan past objections
a fast-food outlet serving people in cars

explanation.definitionFit: To drive a plan through is to force it past objections; a drive-through serves diners in their cars.

clue.text: A few scenes, advising how to resolve court dispute?

definitions.text: advising how to resolve court dispute?
definitions.meaning: in tennis a disputed or obstructed point is replayed: 'play a let'

explanation.definitionFit: A playlet is a short play; in tennis a let means the point is played again.

clue.text: Responding to each other in recitative, man or woman finally compromised

indicators.note: something compromised is damaged or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter, which is the same for man or woman

explanation.surface: A singer of either sex has messed up the sung recitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man or woman finally' gives N either way; 'compromised' shuffles RECITATIVE + N.
explanation.definitionFit: Interactive means acting on one another, each responding to the other.

clue.text: Why one puts fingers to lips? Nonsense!

definitions.text: Why one puts fingers to lips?
definitions.meaning: a finger on the lips is the gesture made to hush, to say sh

explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Kinky senorita game for this lifestyle?

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A raunchy Spanish woman plays games suited to a racy life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' shuffles SENORITA GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A menage a trois is a domestic arrangement of three lovers living together.

clue.text: Quiet acceptance about tryst being a second short

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the letters are left out

parts.note: an assignation is a secret meeting of lovers
A plus S, the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Accepting a lover's date quietly, though a second is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes AS out of ASSIGNATION, leaving SIGNATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Resignation is calm acceptance of something unpleasant.

clue.text: He torments criminal as very backward

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong and bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man inflicts criminal torment, being terribly backward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' shuffles HE TORMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest, furthest down, as far behind or back as possible.

clue.text: 1 dn, in summary

definitions.meaning: points to the phrase meaning nothing more to say

explanation.definitionFit: All told means counting everything up, and likewise signals the end of a tale.

clue.text: Mute, adding nothing to endlessly irritable row

indicators.note: without its end, the word for irritable loses its last letter

parts.note: sore can mean irritated or touchy
a din is a loud noise, a row
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Quiet, adding nothing to a crotchety endless argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SORE to SOR; 'adding nothing to' puts O at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sordino is a mute for a musical instrument, used to soften its tone.

clue.text: Howled out loud, that's plain

indicators.note: said out loud the word matches another

parts.note: to bawl is to howl or cry loudly

explanation.surface: Wailed loudly; that much is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: BAWLED sounds like BALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Bald means blunt or unadorned, as in a bald statement of fact.

clue.text: Wild man going, on and off, for princess

indicators.note: only every other letter is used, alternating between take and skip

explanation.surface: A savage leaves now and then for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of WILD MAN gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
